title: IDSA 2025 Guideline Update on Complicated Urinary Tract Infections
shortTitle: IDSA 2025: shorter cUTI treatment and earlier oral switch
summary: IDSA suggests shorter treatment for improving cUTI: 5–7 days of an effective fluoroquinolone or 7 days of another effective antibiotic. It also supports IV-to-oral transition when patients improve, tolerate oral medication and have an active oral option. Duration starts on the first effective treatment day.
whyItMatters: Use severity, prior cultures and resistance risks to choose empiric therapy, then narrow and reassess route and duration. Bacteremia alone does not require an entire IV course in a stable, source-controlled patient.
limitations: Many supporting studies excluded severe sepsis, obstruction, abscess, catheters and immunocompromise. Suspected prostatitis and unresolved source-control problems need individualized treatment.
population: Adults with complicated UTI, including acute pyelonephritis and selected Gram-negative bacteremia.
intervention: Severity-informed antibiotic selection, oral transition and shorter duration.
comparator: Longer courses or continued parenteral therapy.
findings: Seven days is suggested for improving cUTI with Gram-negative bacteremia.
evidenceNotes: Historical backfill. Official IDSA recommendations and remarks reviewed; linked manuscript evidence tables and supplements were not reviewed. Official release July 17, 2025, rather than later journal issue dates. This is an original synopsis, not a reproduction.
guidelineStrength: Short-course fluoroquinolone: conditional/moderate certainty; other antibiotics: conditional/very low. Oral switch: conditional/low; bacteremic switch: conditional/very low.
